title: Dreams on the Train
subtitle: The world may seem new, but it's never as different as you'd like it to be.

items.text: Dreams on the Train
Passenger Car, Train

items.speaker: Critter Merchant
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen, these young critters, a thousand times cheaper than NewBabel's, are the best guardians for your home!

items.speaker: Critter Merchant
items.text: Specially bred by our top caretakers! You won't find a better deal anywhere!
The merchant holds a confused critter high above his head, pitching it to the passengers as he passes them by.
The carriage is packed shoulder to shoulder, the air thick with sweat and the smell of critters in their cages.
A woman in a faded sari carries a baby strapped to her back. Barefoot men cling tightly to the entrance railings.
Children dart this way and that between the legs of adults, playing hide-and-seek and dodging would-be scoldings.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Wow. There are so many people here. Everyone is trying to be somewhere else ... somewhere new ...

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Staying stuck in one place for so long makes you the rare creature, kid.

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: Nobody wants to stay put forever. Merchants, students, beggars, ascetics ... idiots or clever little pickpockets—everyone wants a peek outside their own little world. Otherwise, how would they ever figure out where they really stand?

items.speaker: Janardhan
items.text: People who never leave home never figure out who they really are.

items.speaker: Teacher
items.text: Excuse me, sir.

items.speaker: Teacher
items.text: Stay close, kids! Eyes forward! No wandering off or stopping!
A teacher raises her hand high, leading a group of children into the carriage.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: Miss, wait ... M-My wallet's gone! My ticket was in there!
A boy digs through his pockets, calling out for help.
But in the chaos of the train, his small voice is swallowed whole.

items.speaker: Student
items.text: It should be here. I swear I put it in my pocket!
He fumbles helplessly, unaware that his teacher and classmates have already left him behind.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: Punji? You saw what happened. That man took it?
The little snake hisses softly by her ear.
Kanjira looks toward the direction of its flicking tongue. A hunched man in a long coat stands there, not at all looking like a thief.
But she steps forward anyway.

items.speaker: Thief
items.text: What's the matter, kid? Starving so bad you've lost your mind? Be smart and back off. This one's my catch.
Before she even speaks, he already figures out who she is.

items.speaker: Kanjira
items.text: No. I just want the wallet back. And the train ticket. You can keep the money.

items.speaker: Thief
items.text: Heh ... And what if I say no? You out here trying to be a saint while picking pockets yourself?
